question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

have your heart in your mouth

options.text: to behave in a foolish manner

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"have your heart in your mouth"** means to be extremely ***frightened or anxious***. (बेहद डरना या चिंतित होना)

 
 
• **Example:** When I saw the car heading straight for me, I had **my heart in my mouth.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is*** 'to be extremely frightened.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: to be extremely jealous** (बेहद ईर्ष्यालु होना)

 
 
• **Example:** She was ***extremely jealous*** when she saw her friend with a new car.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: to behave in a foolish manner** (मूर्खतापूर्ण व्यवहार करना)
 
 
• **Example:** He behaved in a ***foolish manner*** at the party last night.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: to get worse and worse** (बद से बदतर होना)
 
 
• **Example:** His health has been*** getting worse and worse*** since the accident.
